column1: # Known original bugs and deliberate port deviations.
# One row per finding. This is the index a QoL pass works from: every bug the port reproduces is
# here, with the address the evidence came from and where the reproduction lives in the port.
# kind        bug        the original does something wrong
#             residue    the return value is whatever a register happened to hold
#             missing    the original has no test it should have (not-found, out-of-range, no floor)
#             naming     the IDA name describes the function wrongly; behaviour is fine
#             duplicate  the original contains the same function twice
#             deviation  the port deliberately differs from the original
# reproduced  yes   the port reproduces it, and a test asserts it
#             no    the port does NOT reproduce it (a deviation), listed here so it is not lost
#             n/a         the original function is not ported yet
#             unverified  available source/test evidence does not establish a reproduction
# qol         yes   a QoL patch should probably fix this
#             no          fixing it would change intended game behaviour
#             unassessed  no QoL decision is recorded
# Port-side bugs we introduced and fixed are NOT listed here; they are recorded in docs/parity/.
# Removed the false 0x67048 manufacturing-shift claim; see base-removal-compaction-2026-10-28.md.
# Removed false 0x6858C/0x689E4 loot-index claims; see loot-return-indexing-2026-10-28.md.

column4: what_the_original_does
column5: evidence

column4: The facility-type search has no found test. A type no base has leaves the index on the base count, the compaction guard fails, and the function still drops the count and deletes apBases[count-1] - so it removes the LAST base.
column5: Loop exit at 0x66BB0, guard at 0x66E4C, unconditional delete at 0x6715C

column4: When no strateg entry matches, the index equals the item count and StrategList_RemoveAt is called one past the end.
column5: Search loop at 0x66BE4, call at 0x66C58

column4: The argument is used with two meanings in one function: a facility type at 0x66BB8 and a SITE ID at 0x66BE4. Not a bug, but it is why the name is misleading.
column5: 0x66BB8 compares nFacType, 0x66BE4 compares StrategItem.nSiteId

column4: No found test. The search loop ends with the index at the count and 0x36BE0 deletes apSoldiers[count], one slot past the array, and decrements the count anyway.
column5: 0x36BE0 store against the loop-exit index

column4: Removing items while walking forward skips entries, so a purge pass does not remove everything it should.
column5: Forward walk against a shrinking array

column4: Only subtracts when the byte is already non-zero, but has no floor: 30 minus 40 becomes 246. It also does not check the found index, so it can touch abGrid[-1].
column5: 0x6ACEC body

column4: Returns the constant 1620, which is whatever R0 happened to hold.
column5: 0x6ACEC return

column4: No sentinel test on the craft index, so asking for craft 255 counts the soldiers who are aboard nothing.
column5: 0x6649C compares bUnk183 against the argument with no bound

column4: Charges 50,000 per month for every facility cell whose TYPE byte is not 255, and never checks build days. An unfinished facility is charged the full amount, the opposite of every capacity function in the same family.
column5: 0x6A230 reads the type grid only

column4: The original contains the same search twice: 0x5A8D0 and 0x6AC30 search BaseRec.bUnk4 and return -1, differing only in bounds. The port keeps one implementation and deliberately does not cite 0x5A8D0.
column5: 0x5A8D0 versus 0x6AC30

column4: The name says it clears a grid row. It clears nothing: it classifies a base and stores a state byte into 0x161F38.
column5: 0x6A0E0 body

column4: Returns 6 no matter what it did: the inner counter is reset to 0 on every row and always runs to 6. It also calls Base_CalcWorkshopCap at 0x65BC0 and discards the result.
column5: 0x65C20 reset, 0x65BC0 discarded call

column4: Retracted skip-one analysis: the original removes matching IDs from the global Soldier pool, while tactical side-list counts are reloaded but not overwritten. The port now uses the global pool and authoritative count.
column5: Raw ARM 0x36BB4 overwrites incoming R0 with Map base; 0x36C4C updates the global count; side loops at 0x3DD40 and 0x3DDFC reload counts without storing the return.

column4: Slot 34 is asymmetric: the base is charged 5 per unit and the craft is credited 50. The same asymmetry appears on the landing path at 0x68948, so it is the game's rule rather than a hangar-screen quirk - listed because it looks like a bug and a QoL pass will be asked about it.
column5: 0x7AC38 and 0x68948

column4: The original falls back to a rolled v124.dat read when the primary read fails. The port reproduces the roll but not the file-level retry, because the port's asset reader has no equivalent.
column5: 0x44248 fallback branch

column4: The original resolves the palette as 0x1472D0 + 256 * (Map.paletteBase + slot), where paletteBase is a dword read out of the Map block. The port indexes g_aPalette[(nPal + 0) & (PUFO_PAL_SLOTS - 1)] - the +0 is a placeholder for that Map-resident base, which the port does not model yet.
column5: 0x9EC48 decompile, palette index expression

column4: Every 5-6-5 field is scaled with (f * key) >> 8. With key = 255 that is (f * 255) >> 8, which is f - 1 for every non-zero field, so a fully opaque blend still loses one unit in red, green and blue. dst 0xFFFF blended with colour 0xFFFF at key 255 gives 0xF7DE, never 0xFFFF.
column5: 0xA460C blend expression; test_render asserts 0xF7DE

column4: nKey = 0 does not mean "leave the destination alone". The inverse factor is 255 - 0 = 255, so the existing pixel is scaled by 255/256 and every non-zero field drops by one. dst 0x001F with key 0 becomes 0x001E.
column5: 0xA4590 computes 255 - nKey before the loop; test_render asserts 0x001E

column4: The original stores the transparency index in a global (blitColorKey @ 0xa3028) that SoftSurf_BlitIndexedKeyed_Inner reads for every glyph byte. The port keeps the setter but its keyed blit takes the key as a parameter, so nothing in the port reads the stored value.
column5: 0xA3728 and 0xA3840 load blitColorKey and BEQ past the write on a glyph-byte match

column4: The bounds test is x <= nSurf0 and y <= nSurf1, not <. A coordinate equal to the dimension is accepted: sampling at x == width reads the first pixel of the next row, and at y == height it reads past the end of the surface buffer.
column5: 0xA4630 bounds compares; test_render asserts SamplePixel(4,0) on a 4-wide surface returns the next row's pixel

column4: The same 420-byte body appears twice in the original, at 0xa3a14 as Blit_CopyRows and at 0xa3db8 as SoftSurf_BlitCopyRaw: same three pixel-mode branches, same loop bodies. The port keeps one implementation and cites both addresses.
column5: Both decompilations are identical line for line; both are 420 bytes in docs/idb/inventory-grouped.tsv

column4: The 24bpp branch writes three bytes per pixel (LDRH/STRH then LDRB/STRB) but advances the destination by only two (ADD R7,R7,#2), while the row step at 0xa3614 is 3 * nSurf0. Pixels overlap each other and a row of n of them covers 2n bytes of a 3n-byte row.
column5: Disassembly at 0xa35e4; test_render asserts the second pixel starts at +2 and that byte 5 of the row is never written

column4: Named SoftSurf_BlitIndexed_Mode12 in the IDB although nothing in it indexes a palette: it copies the glyph's own pixel values into the loaded surface. Renamed in the IDB to SoftSurf_BlitRawGlyph. IDA reports no cross-references to it, and the same is true of SoftSurf_BlitCopyRaw @ 0xa3db8 and SoftSurf_SamplePixel @ 0xa4630.
column5: set_type and rename applied in the IDB; xrefs_to 0xa33c8 returns none

column4: The character index is var34[v41 + v34], where v34 is the line number. Line 0 draws from character 0, line 1 from character 1, line 2 from character 2 - each line drops as many leading characters as its own index, even though each line is a different 205-byte text record. With the count formula (cursor - line - 1) the result is a diagonal reveal, not a typewriter.
column5: 0x26E14 loads v35[v41 + v34]; the loop at 0x26EF0 advances the record pointer by 205 per line while v34 also increments

column4: The right border strip is drawn at nX + nWidth, one pixel outside the body the fill just covered, while the left border sits at nX. The dialog frame is therefore one pixel wider on the right than the filled area.
column5: 0x265D4 blits at v9 + nWidth where v9 = (240 - nWidth)/2 and the fill at 0x26538 covers nWidth from v9

column4: The original copies a text record into a 92-byte stack buffer (var34[92]) with no length check, so a record longer than 91 characters corrupts the stack. The port uses a 205-byte buffer, the full record size.
column5: var34[92] at bp-34h; the copy loop at 0x26DB0 runs until the terminator with no bound

column4: Ten text records are copied one after another into the caller's scratch buffer by byte loops with no length check, so a long record corrupts whatever follows it. The port uses PUFO_TEXT_REC_STRIDE, the full record size.
column5: copy loops at 0x20F44, 0x20F98, 0x21008, 0x2107C, 0x210CC, 0x21104, 0x21140, 0x21178, 0x211B0 and 0x211EC all write through pIso->szText with no bound

column4: The action-latch switch handles modes 2, 3 and 4 and sends every other value above 1 to the draw with nGlyphA never assigned, so the marker is drawn with whatever glyph index the previously drawn cell left in the shared context. Mode 0 and 1 take a defined path; 5 and above do not.
column5: default branch at 0x1B324 goes to LABEL_27, and the only writes to pIso->nGlyphA before it are at 0x1B384 (mode 3) and 0x1B40C

column4: Same shape in the high marker: an action-latch value that is not 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 jumps straight to the draw with a stale nGlyphA and nGlyphB left at zero.
column5: goto LABEL_35 at 0x1B608

column4: The gate tests the whole dword at Map+0x14000 while the glyph index reads the same place with LDRH. A value that is only non-zero in the high half passes the gate and then contributes nothing to the index, so the glyph drawn is the one the low half alone selects.
column5: Gate at 0x1C2B4 is a dword load, the index at 0x1C674 uses LDRH R3, [R7, R12]

column4: The mode 1 team rule loads the selected base byte with LDRSB and compares it against the unsigned Soldier base-index byte at +0xB6. A selected-base value of 0x80 or more sign-extends to a negative int and matches no unsigned byte, so the tactical roster comes out empty. Base indices are small in practice, so the quirk is latent.
column5: 0x398B8 LDRSB R2, [R1, R12] loads 0x159D81; 0x398BC LDRB R3, [R0, #0xB6] loads the Soldier byte; 0x398C0 CMP R3, R2 compares them

column4: The 24-bit branch reads HIBYTE(w) and the low byte of w, so it only ever sees the low 16 bits of a palette entry, and it writes back a 16-bit value. Palette_Load packs the 0x100 format as R | G<<8 | B<<16, so on a 24-bit display this pass drops the whole blue channel out of every palette. Harmless on the 16bpp devices the game shipped on, which is probably why it survived.
column5: ARM at 0x37718 uses HIBYTE(v5) and at 0x37760 (u8)v5; the store at 0x377BC writes the repacked 16-bit value back over the 4-byte slot

column4: operator new is not checked. The null is stored into Map.apSoldiers at 0x22BF0 and dereferenced on the next instruction at 0x22C10, so a failed allocation is a crash rather than a behaviour. There is also no bounds check on the roster array; the index is the low half of a u16 count.
column5: No test between 0x22BC0 and 0x22C10. apSoldiers[LOWORD(nSoldierCount)] written at 0x22BF0, then [count]->nUnk440 at 0x22C10

column4: The roster is freed with operator delete without nulling the slots and without clearing the count. If FindChunk or the 2-byte count read fails, nSoldierCount still names memory that has already been freed, and the next pass through the roster frees it again.
column5: Free loop at 0x430FC writes nothing back; the only early exits are 0x43124 and 0x4313C, both after the free loop

column4: The third pickup stores the selected unit, the hit item and the pointer position, but unlike the two slot passes (0x3BF38, 0x3C1D8) and the ammo pickup (0x3C3EC) it never zeroes nInvDragOffX/Y. It inherits the footprint offset the previous re-test left, so a 2-wide item picked up just before leaves -20, the re-test lands at 150,150 which is inside no hit rect at all, and the slot it was aiming at is missed.
column5: 0x3C4C8 writes pSelUnit, 0x3C4D0 writes pInvHitItem, 0x3C4DC and 0x3C4EC write the pointer from aInvHitRects[10]; there is no store to Map+0x4A28 or Map+0x4A2C anywhere in that block

column4: Only the fallback slot-index swap at 0x3C0F0 is unreachable. The first gate at 0x3BF9C skips this pass when the equipped slot's nIndex equals the wanted byte. The fallback walk repeats that same equality at 0x3BFFC, so it cannot branch to 0x3C0F0 on the unequal fallthrough. This is separate from the live sort-key match at 0x3BFC4 -> 0x3C014, which moves the item identity and ammo and is covered by TestEquipSlotSwap case 1.
column5: 0x3BF98 CMP slot nIndex,wanted / 0x3BF9C BEQ 0x3C110; 0x3BFFC CMP same pair / 0x3C000 BEQ 0x3C0F0; 0x3BFC0 CMP candidate sort key,wanted / 0x3BFC4 BEQ 0x3C014; TestEquipSlotSwap case1 checks pool creation, item identity, rounds and removal

column4: auStat[8] is the divisor of the carry gate and is reached through __rt_sdiv with no zero test, so a soldier with strength 0 divides by zero. auStat[8] is loaded with LDRH, so it is the unsigned 16-bit stat, and abUnk1012 is a byte array while TactItem.nIndex is a u16, making the compare 16-bit against 8-bit.
column5: 0x3C280 LDRH R0,[R7,#0xB2] then 0x3C298 LDR R3,=_rt_sdiv / MOV PC,R3

column4: When the last soldier in the roster has nUnitType 6, which is the soldier object index 33 just created, the loop skips its ammo computation and writes nAmmo = 0 into apTactItems[nTactItemCount]: a slot this iteration has not created yet. In shipped memory that slot is whatever the pointer array holds past the count.
column5: ARM 0x39A14 is LDRH count / ADD R3,R5,R3,LSL#2 / LDR R3,[R3,#0x1194] / LDRB R3,[R3,#0xA0] / CMP R3,#6; 0x39A5C stores 0 through apTactItems[Map_nTactItemCount] and jumps to the shared tail at 0x39B20

column4: The hardware ammo switch has cases 31, 32, 34 and 35 with default: break, so object index 33 never assigns the ammo total. The split at the end of the copy loop then reuses whatever total the previous object index left, so hardware soldiers from object 33 carry the wrong clip size.
column5: 0x39A68 is the switch; 0x39B20 is the default break that every path converges on; 0x39D50 and 0x39D98 read the same stack slot var_C that only cases 31, 32, 34 and 35 write

column4: The fourth race group's count is read from stack slot var_24, which the function never writes. The group it bounds is the one that gets Map_abSpriteSet[3], so the fourth sprite set is handed out based on whatever a previous frame left at SP+0x6C.
column5: var_24 has exactly two references in the whole 3516-byte function: the frame declaration and this LDR. The bound it feeds is CMP R7, (var_24 + var_28 + var_2C + var_30) at 0x3A8CC, and the group body at 0x3A8DC loads Map_abSpriteSet+3

column4: The alien set index is stored for mission mode 0, 1, 2 and 3 but the BNE at 0x3A2F0 leaves the slot unwritten for any mode above 3, and that index then selects a row of the eight-row composition table and of the eight-entry mission totals table.
column5: 0x3A31C (mode 0), 0x3A30C (mode 1), 0x3A304 (mode 2) and 0x3A2F4 (mode 3, R2 preloaded to 5) all store it; 0x3A2F0 is the fall-through that stores nothing; 0x3A338 overwrites it when nMissionType is 9

column4: nPal is saved on the stack at entry and zeroed when the unit is operative, but only the paths that pass the visibility gate write it back. A small operative unit on an unflagged cell, and a large operative unit with no flagged cell anywhere in its 2 by 2 block, jump straight to the POP and leave IsoDrawCtx.nPal at 0 for the caller, which reuses it for the terrain glyphs.
column5: 0x1CA58 (large, after the four bFlags44 tests) and the small path after the re-test at 0x1CA50 both branch to 0x1D5E4, which is ADD SP,SP,#8 / POP {R4-R11,PC}; the restore lives only at 0x1D5DC, LDR R3,[SP,#8+var_4] then STR R3,[R4,#0x6C]

column4: The weapon overlay chooses its object by a fall-through chain: the selected weapon, then a left-hand weapon, then a right-hand weapon, then the left hand's object, then the right hand's object. With BOTH hands empty the last step is LDREQ R3,[R2] with R2 = 0, a null dereference. Nothing in the function tests pHandR before that load.
column5: 0x1D344 loads pHandR and 0x1D34C tests it null and branches straight to 0x1D37C; 0x1D37C is CMP R3,#0 / LDRNE R3,[R3] / LDREQ R3,[R2], and 0x1D388 then reads [R3,#0xA0]

column4: The two-hand weapon offset is read as aUnitFacingDrawOff[2*(8*nUnitType + bFacing)] and that table is 224 bytes: 14 unit types, not 23. A unit of type 14 or above reaching this branch reads past the table into the u16 table at 0xA9488 that Map_TraceVoxelOccupancy (0x3242c) indexes as 4*(8*nUnitType + bFacing).
column5: 0x1D288..0x1D294 is LDRB R2,[R5,#5] / LDRB R3,[R5,#0xA0] / ADD R3,R2,R3,LSL#3 / ADD R3,R0,R3,LSL#1 / LDRSB R3,[R3] with no bound test; aUnitFacingDrawOff ends at 0xA9488

column4: The cell-grid allocator stores the result of operator new(0x3C) whether or not it succeeded, then calls MapCell_Init on the same pointer. MapCell_Init has no null guard, so a failed allocation is a write to address zero.
column5: 0x22EF4 MOV R3,#0x15338 is the store base; the loop stores the new pointer at Map+0x15338 + 4*(60*nY+nX) + 0x3840*nLayer and calls MapCell_Init with it unconditionally; only the MapCell_Reset call is guarded

column4: The tail masks every cell's nFlags32 with 0xFFFFFF87 through the loaded cell pointer with no null test, so one cell the allocator failed to produce is a crash.
column5: 0x25740 MOV R3,#0x15338; the walk loads the cell dword and ANDs [cell+32] with no CMP against zero anywhere in 0x2571C..0x257B0

column4: The craft pad name is aPlane[9*(Map_nMissionType - 1)] with no test for mission type 0, so a type 0 mission reads nine bytes before aPlane, landing in the zero padding between aAlienSecondaryCounts and aHwpsDeployOffsets.
column5: 0x231EC LDR R0,=aPlane with the index formed as 9*Map_nMissionType - 9; aPlane starts at 0xA6668 and aAlienSecondaryCounts ends at 0xA6667

column4: The UFO module name index 3*(Map_nTerrainVariant-1) + Map_nMissionTier is not bounded against the 15-slot aUfo1a: a variant above 5, or a tier above 2, reads past the table into the alien tables. The port yields an empty name instead, which fails the .ma1 load the way a missing member does.
column5: 0x2303C and 0x236DC LDR R3,=aUfo1a; aUfo1a ends at 0xA6617 and aAlienRaceCounts starts at 0xA6618

column4: The loader sizes each block as operator new(2 * (AssetReader_Size() / 2)) and then reads the FULL member size into it, so an odd member overflows the allocation by one byte. It also overwrites the two globals without freeing what the previous load left, so a reload leaks the first pair.
column5: 0x3BDA8 operator new(2*(size/2)) then 0x3BDC0 AssetReader_Read(pBuf, AssetReader_Size()); same pair at 0x3BDF0 / 0x3BE10; neither site frees the old pointer

column4: The layer switch writes var_350 / var_354 only for a layer count of 1, 2 or 3. Zero skips the consumer, but 4 or more reach the showship reveal centre with values this function never wrote.
column5: 0x3CE70 switch on Map_nMapLayers: 1 and 3 store (5,10), 2 stores (5,5), there is no default; var_350 / var_354 are read at 0x3CEA4

column4: When operator new(0x14) for the briefing pad fails, the code stores the prologue's zero register into unk_15692C and calls PadImage_Load anyway; 0x3D2E8 then writes through the stored NULL.
column5: 0x3D2B8 CMP R0,#0 and 0x3D2BC BEQ loc_3D2CC; 0x3D2CC MOV R0,R11 where R11 is the zero set at 0x3C598; 0x3D2E8 STR R11,[R0]

column4: The briefing pad global unk_15692C is overwritten without freeing what the previous mission allocated: with zero on the skip path at 0x3D548, and with the new pad at 0x3D2D0.
column5: 0x3D548 LDR R0,=0x15692C then STR R11,[R0]; 0x3D2D0 STR R0,[R5]; neither site frees the old pointer

column4: AssetReader_Find for showship.dat is not tested, so a missing member leaves the reader size at zero and the code allocates zero bytes that the reveal block then reads its two header words through. The port stores NULL for a zero-size member, which the reveal block already treats as nothing to reveal.
column5: 0x3CADC LDR R1,=aShowshipDat with no test on the AssetReader_Find result; AssetReader_Size feeds operator new; the header words are read at 0x3CEA4

column4: Its first argument is the facility grid the caller wants written, and the function never reads it: every store goes through the global 0x159768. Both callers pass the grid they mean, so the difference is latent.
column5: 0x623BC takes 6 arguments; R0 is overwritten at 0x623C0 by the bClear load and never used, while 0x62428 and 0x624B8 load 0x159768 directly

column4: Nothing bounds nBaseIndex, nX, nY or nFacType. aFacBuildSpec has 18 three-byte records, so a facility type of 18 or more reads past it, and a base index of 8 writes past the 1524-byte grid.
column5: 0x623E8 forms 3*nFacType + aFacBuildSpec with no test; 0x62418 forms 24*nBase + nY with no test

column4: The hangar (type 11) is a 2 by 2 footprint: it marks all four tileA quadrants 9, 10, 11 and 12 but gives build days to only three of them. The ARM reaches the day bytes as +0, +1 and +7 from the anchor, and +7 is the diagonal, so the (nY+1,nX) cell never gets one.
column5: 0x6247C STRB R4,[R5,R3]!; 0x62480 STRB R4,[R5,#1]; 0x62484 STRB R4,[R5,#7] against 0x62438/0x62444/0x62458/0x62460, which do cover all four quadrants

column4: The return value is 6*(24*nBase + nY + 18), the address delta the facType store used. It is register residue, not a status, and no caller uses it.
column5: 0x624F8 MUL R0,R11,R0 with R11 = R7 + 0x12, then POP {R4-R11,PC}

column4: With the grant flag clear the function adds nothing and returns its own first argument, which is otherwise unused; the base it grants to comes from the global at Map+0x1174.
column5: 0x95FA8 MOV R3,R1,LSL#24 / MOVS / BEQ locret_96018; locret_96018 is POP {R4,PC} with R0 unchanged

column4: The hangar scan's second test reads fac[nBase].layer2[1][result+1] -- row 1, always -- while the stamp it authorises goes to layer2[v10+1][result+1]. For any row below the first, the cell that was tested and the cell that is written are different cells.
column5: 0x2CC1C ADD R11,R6,R0 / 0x2CC28 ORR R10,R10,#3 / 0x2CC2C LDRB R11,[R11,R10] with R10 = 0x1C3 and no v10 term, against 0x2CDA0 STRB R2,[R3,#0x4F] which does carry v10

column4: The scan runs v10 and result over 0..4 only, so it searches a 5 by 5 corner of a 6 by 6 grid: a hangar cell in the last row or the last column is never found.
column5: 0x2CC18 CMP R0,#5 and 0x2CCD8 CMP R1,#5 against a 36-byte layer

column4: A craft type outside 0..4 matches the cell and writes Ship.bHangarX and bHangarY, then falls through the switch into the inner loop increment: nothing is stamped, the loop keeps going, and the coordinates from the unmatched match stay written.
column5: 0x2CC9C..0x2CCBC five CMP/BEQ pairs with no default, falling into 0x2CCC0 ADD R0,R0,#1 / CMP R0,#5 / BLT loc_2CC0C

column4: When operator new(0x44) fails the code still stores the NULL into apCraft and still bumps the id and the count; if the scan then matches, 0x2CC8C writes the hangar column through that NULL.
column5: 0x2CB38 CMP R0,#0 / BEQ loc_2CB5C, and loc_2CB5C is MOV R0,#0 into the same store path at 0x2CB7C

column4: The return value is the inner counter: the column index on a match, and 5 when nothing matched. No caller uses it.
column5: 0x2CDA4 is the single return block reached from both the match at 0x2CDA0 and the loop exit at 0x2CCDC, with R0 unchanged

column4: The throw branch tests only bTrajHitStop and then dereferences pArrowThrownItem (Map+0x14070) and its pObj with no null check, so a flag set without a stored item is a crash. The port keeps the same unguarded dereference; no test can cover the null path.
column5: 0x1BDC8 LDRB byte_127A25 / BEQ loc_1C238, then 0x1C1F4 LDR R1,[R5,#0x14070] and 0x1C1F8 LDR R3,[R1] with nothing tested between them

column4: The nudge index 10 * Map.nRowId + n is not bounded. nRowId is the raw aim class id Tact_ComputeAimVector stores at Map+0x14088, so an id above 5 reads past the 64-byte nudge table: ids 6 and 7 land in the second copy of it, higher ids land in the tables after that.
column5: 0x1BD18 MUL R3,R2,#0xA then ADD LR,R3,R1 with no CMP anywhere in 0x1BD10..0x1BD60, and 0x305C0 STR R0,[R4,#0x14088] storing nFlags unclamped

column4: The 64-byte glyph nudge table is stored twice in the image, byte_A9290 for x and byte_A92D0 for y, byte for byte identical. The port keeps one copy and audits both addresses against it.
column5: docs/parity/audit_tables.py compares 0xA9290 and 0xA92D0 against the single g_abArrowGlyphOff, both exact

column4: The return value is whatever register the last branch left. MapView_DrawIsoLayer drops it: it reloads pIso into R0 on the very next instruction. The port returns the number of glyphs drawn instead.
column5: 0x21FC8 BL MapView_DrawUnitFacingArrow followed by 0x21FCC MOV R0,R4

column4: The x/y cell divide (MOVS / ADDMI #0xF / ASR #4) is truncating division, not floor: -17 gives -1, not -2. For v < 0, (v + 15) >> 4 equals v / 16 exactly. column4: The progress column divides BEFORE it multiplies, and ResearchScreen_RefreshPanels does the opposite, so the same topic on the same data shows a different percentage depending on which function last drew it. BuildPanels: 0x73834 LDRH R1,[R10,#0xA] as the dividend, 0x73850 LDRH R0,[R10,#8] as the divisor, _rt_sdiv, then 0x73870 MUL R0,R3,#0x64 on the QUOTIENT -- 100 * (wProgress / wTotal). RefreshPanels: 0x73168 MUL R1,R2,#0x64 on the dividend, then the sdiv at 0x73184 -- (100 * wProgress) / wTotal. A topic one quarter done therefore reads 0% when the panels are built and 25% after any refresh, which is what the player sees when the screen updates under a running topic. Both also divide by wTotal with no test.

The column clear that follows the unlock roll re-clears the FINISHED topic's eight per-base entries instead of the newly unlocked topic's, so a topic can be unlocked while still carrying a stale allocation. ResearchScreen_AccumulateAllocated (0x74914) books auResearchCol[i] into wProgress for every i below the entry count, locked topics included, so the stale entry is not hypothetical.

column4: The panels-not-built half of the buy/sell frame dereferences all five buy/sell panels after BuySellScreen_BuildPanels' teardown has deleted them, and it reads the row marker without subtracting the 2000 alien offset. BuySellScreen_BuildPanels (0x76de0) tears the panels down at 0x77D60..0x77E38 -- UiPanel_FreeLines plus operator delete for A, B, E, C, D -- and never nulls pBuySellPanelA..E; the last thing the teardown does is the funds rollback STRNE at 0x77E50. column4: The round a shot consumes is gated only on the projectile offset being 0 and on the -1 "unlimited" sentinel. The -2 "no weapon on this mount" sentinel is not exempt. A mount whose id is outside 25..30 -- 24, the psi amplifier, is the one the shipped data uses -- stores a zero weapon range in RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament, so once the radar's reach falls to 0 the engage byte is set and the cooldown stays at 255 (nothing ever lands, so nothing rearms it downward). The mount's switch in DrawOverlay has no arm for that id, so the projectile offset is never advanced and the "a shot started" test stays true on every frame: the ammo counter walks off through -3, -4, -5 ... without bound, and DrawCraftArmament's label test is `!= -2`, so the radar screen starts drawing the runaway number where an ammo count should be.

column4: The full-zoom exit cannot clear the OTHER craft chasing the same contact. Ship_ClearInterceptByStrategIdx at 0x61434 is reached through BLEQ, so it runs only when the zero flag is set; the only path that arrives with it set is 0x61428 LDRB bRadarTraceLost / 0x6142C LDRBEQ bRadarFlip / 0x61430 ANDSEQ, i.e. bRadarTraceLost == 0 AND bRadarFlip == 0. But the gate that let this block run at all, 0x613BC, already requires bRadarFlip != 0. So when an intercept reaches full zoom with the trace still held, only nInterceptShipIdx is retargeted at 0x613EC and every other craft with bIntercepting set and the same nStrategIdx keeps chasing a contact the radar screen has given up on.

The same byte is a 0..7 size class in the flag-0x14 arm, so no single bound fits both roles. The port bounds it against PUFO_MISSION_SITE_COUNT.

column4: The byte at +0x02 carries two unrelated roles and nothing in the binary says so: a 0..7 size class on a spawned contact (the 0x90A8C jumptable maps it onto TEXTS 1359..1363) and a mission-site index on an intercept item, because BasePlaneScreen_AddInterceptMission stores the index of the site it is adding into this same byte. column4: The flag-0x15 city line dereferences whatever PtrArray_Get returns, with no null test. PtrArray_Get @ 0xA1130 returns 0 for a negative index (0xA1134 BMI -> 0xA114C MOV R0,#0) and 0 for an index at or above the stored count (the LDRLT pair at 0xA1140/0xA1144 only runs when the compare said less-than, otherwise 0xA114C sets R0 to 0), so any colour-slot byte outside the strateg list makes 0x91798 `LDR R3,[R0,#0x84]` read from address 0x84. The colour byte is a u8 and the list is bounded by whatever the scenload left in it, so nothing here guarantees the range.

column4: StrategItem.nTargetIdx is a signed dword and it indexes the 56-record mission-site table straight after `MUL R2,R3,#0x18` and `ADD R3,R2,R7+0xC8`, with no bound on either side: 56..0x7FFFFFFF reads past the end of aMissionSites @ 0x1865C0 and any negative value reads before it (the port proves the second half by putting a named record in the slot in front of its own copy of the table). The 0x13 arm's version of the same line (0x90E94) is unbounded the same way but reads the +0x02 BYTE, which at least cannot go below -128.

The flag-0x16 arm (0x91938..0x91B1C) is a copy of the flag-0x17 arm (0x914A4..0x91688): 484 bytes and 121 instructions each, same order, same frame slots, same callees. 117 pairs disassemble identically and the 4 that differ are equivalent -- three copy-loop BNEs naming their own loop head and `STRB R2,[R0,R1]` (0x91AE4) against `STRB R2,[R1,R0]` (0x91650), the same additive address. Nothing observable depends on the copy; the cost is 484 bytes and a second place to fix when the first is wrong.

column4: The soldier name editor changes its DRAW/BLIT ORDER on a flag. With bTransferFlag @ 0x159E10 set it calls SoldierScreen_Draw first and blits its three controls after; with the flag clear it blits the three controls first and calls SoldierScreen_Draw last. The callee is the name-entry readout (screen id 5), so in the unarmed path the readout is painted OVER the three soldier-find buttons it has just blitted, and in the armed path the buttons come on top of the same readout. Nothing in the binary says which order is wanted. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapeSoldierArms pins it through the pfnTextInput seam (0 blits armed, 3 unarmed)

column4: The top and bottom rails are 24 steps of 5 with the SAME climbing start (x k+1) but two different falling starts: k+128 on top, k+120 on the bottom. The top row therefore leaves a 7-pixel hole at x 121..127 and its last two rects (k 22 at x 238..242, k 23 at x 243..247) fall past the 240-pixel surface, while the bottom row's ramps meet at x 120 and its last rect ends at x 239. Reproduced as written; a QoL build would use #0x80 in both. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapeBaseFacArm probes x 121..127 dark and x 239 lit.

column4: The two page controls are looped with the index kept in the SHARED scratch counter dword_186B08: stored 0 at 0x92D6C, re-read and incremented per step (0x92D84..0x92D8C), left at 2 when the arm ends. The port uses a local counter, so the residue is not reproduced. Harmless in practice because every other user of that global initialises it first (Ui_OpenBaseInfo 0x84B60, Geoscape_PrepScreenOpen 0x851FC, Geoscape_InitUI's pad loop 0x866B4), but it is a real difference. The same shape runs in case 3 at 0x940B0..0x940D0 (also left at 2) and in case 19 at 0x94338..0x9436C; both are ported with a local counter too.

column4: The hangar's stat panel advances its shared row counter twice for every row that has a count: 0x93498/0x9349C add one whatever the count says, and 0x93600..0x93608 add a second one when the count is above zero. The six rows therefore sit at y 112, 152, 192, 232, 272, 312 instead of 112, 132, ..., 212 -- each with a 20-pixel hole above it -- and 0x93CE8 sizes the three column rails from the same counter, so they are 20*(6+matched) tall: 40 to 140 pixels longer than the panel they border. Reproduced exactly as the ARM does; no row spacing or rail length is 'corrected'.

column4: The cursor block MOVES the map cursor while drawing. Cell kind 10 (Mind Shield) or 12 (Gravity shield) decrements nSmapTapX @ 0x186B7C (0x92458/0x9245C) and kind 11 (Hangar) or 12 decrements nSmapTapY @ 0x186B80 (0x92450/0x92454); kind 9 (Hyper Wave Decoder) moves neither. Both are stored back (0x925A0/0x925A4) and the 64x64 cursor is positioned from the MOVED tap, so the draw relocates the placement cursor one cell up and/or left and every later reader -- the click handler, the next frame -- sees the moved value. Reproduced exactly; no draw-only variant is invented.

column5: 0x929BC..0x929D8 build the pair with R5 loaded from =0x159768; 0x929C0 is the STR. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapePlacementArm compares palette slot 2 entry 27 against Gfx_PackRgb565Pair(&color, 0xFF,0xFF,0xFF, 104,104,104) after a panel run; the mutant WHITE_LOW 104 -> 100 is caught there.

column4: The panel's second triple reads TEXTS 80, 81 and 82 centred on 120 at y 108, 125, 142 (17 apart: 0x92A24 MOV R2,#0x6C, then 0x92A7C and 0x92AC8) -- and all three records are EMPTY in the shipped lang.dat, so half of the failure panel never draws. Kept as the original has it; the test fills the three records to prove the path is live and to pin its three rows.
column5: 0x929DC..0x92ADC walk the three records with the 17-pixel step. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapePlacementArm asserts the empty state paints nothing below row 144 and that filling 80..82 paints rows 111, 128 and 145 (the font's ink band starts three rows under the y it is given).

column4: Three indexes in the cursor block are unbounded. 0x92710 MOV R11,#0x1C with the MUL at 0x92740 and the ADD at 0x92744 index aBaseFacFlags @ 0x186E48 (28-byte records, 17 of them) with the CELL BYTE whatever it says -- a 0xFF cell reads 2,380 bytes past the table. 0x923EC..0x9241C forms the cursor-cell address 6*(24*base + tapY + 62) + tapX with no test on either tap, and 0x9230C ADD R7,R3,LSL#6 with 0x92310 ADD #0x1A indexes aSiteRecs @ 0x186C40 with (char)nSelectedBaseIdx. The port bounds the flags index to PUFO_BASEFAC_COUNT, clamps the grid index into PUFO_GRID_SIZE and the base index into PUFO_FAC_BASE_COUNT.
column5: 0x92740 MUL / 0x92744 ADD [=0x186E48]; 0x923F0 MOV R2,#0x18, 0x923F8 MUL, 0x9240C ADD #0x3E, 0x92414 MUL #6, 0x92418 ADD, 0x9241C LDRB [R3,R5]; 0x9230C/0x92310. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapePlacementArm runs a cell byte of 200 (no label, control still positioned from a zero label width) so the bounded read is observable.

column4: The ten action captions run at 0x92070..0x92290 BEFORE the two grid callees (0x922B4 BaseFacScreen_DrawNameGrid, 0x922C0 Base_DrawFacilityIconStrip), and the name grid's 6x6 blank backdrop (0x61CA4..0x61CC8: 36 basebits glyphs at the scroll origin, every pixel index 0, so palette slot 3 entry 0 is what lands there) paints solid over whatever lies under its 32x32 cells. With the scroll origin at (6,60) those cells reach y 287 and cover caption rows 229, 247 and 265 of BOTH columns -- only the 283 and 301 rows survive on screen. Order and coverage reproduced as the ARM has them.
column5: 0x92294 MOV R0,#3 / 0x922AC STR, then 0x922B0 MOV R0,R5 / 0x922B4 BL and 0x922C0 BL; the backdrop is 0x61CA4..0x61CC8. tests/test_geoscape.c:TestGeoscapePlacementArm measures the captions with the grid origin parked at (0,0) (cells y 36..227, every caption row visible) and pins each inked span against a reference centred draw; with the origin at (6,60) the first three rows of each column produce no ink at all.

Its callers still pass it -- 0x8C294 MOV R0,R8 hands over exactly the byte the callee then re-loads. The port's RadarUpdateEnv.pbActive is the same byte, so the port reads it as the callee does.

column4: With bRadarScreenActive set, cases 0 and 2 skip the map chrome (0x8C2B0), the crosshair (0x8C69C) AND the status panel (0x8C760): 0x8C220 BEQ jumps the whole map arm and 0x8C29C B def_8C1B0 goes straight to the frame end. The radar frame is the strip pad, thirteen root widgets, one blended rect and the radar session -- so the overlay drift, the scroll wrap, the crosshair cooldown and the panel controls all keep whatever the last non-radar frame left them.

column4: The world record behind 0x186BC0 is allocated as 0x4E204 = 4 + 800*400 and memset whole, and its 320000 index bytes are never written by anything in the binary. They are read: Geoscape_Draw @ 0x8C590, RadarScreen_BlitMapBackdrop @ 0x5EBF0 and Geoscape_DrawScreen @ 0x6C250 all pass the record as SoftSurf_BlitFlip's glyph (header at +0, index at +4), so the geoscape world layer paints aPalette slot 29 entry 0 wherever the layer pad's mask allows. No save chunk carries them -- Save_ReadSmap reads the camera, four scalars, the 200 site records and 21 tail bytes only.
column5: 47-xref census on 0x186BC0 (InitUI alloc/memset/pair, the two zoom pair publishes, the three BlitFlip readers, Save_ReadSmap, GeoscapeUi_FreeAll); test_geoiinit asserts the index bytes are zero after InitUI

column4: The arrow handlers take the item slot from panel C's selected row (0x962D0) but re-read dword_186BE8 on each pass (0x96368) to choose the branch and aux/site row. If that global row differs from panel C's row, the item slot and pending row can disagree. A stale row is possible on the first arrow tap while the transfer picker flag is still set: pointer-down hits only the shared confirm control (0x88950), but pointer-up clicks panels B/C before checking that flag (0x8A64C..0x8A680). A prior hangar or shop action can therefore leave dword_186BE8 stale for that tap. After the transfer draw hits a different base and clears the picker flag (0x98980..0x989E0), pointer-down can reach the panel-A row cache (0x96E30), so the stale row is not permanent. Transfer_MoveOneItem has the same cached-row dependence on its left-arrow path (0x9606C, 0x9610C, 0x96254).
column5: 0x962D0 reads panel A aux by panel C's selected row; 0x96368 loads dword_186BE8; 0x96494 writes the selected item slot while 0x964A8/0x964C8 index by the cached row; pointer-up calls panel B/C at 0x8A64C/0x8A66C before the picker gate at 0x8A674; panel-A cache is on the flag-clear path; TransferScreen_Draw clears the flag only when the hit base differs from source (0x989D0..0x989E0)

column4: dword_186BE8, the row the arrow handlers work on, is ONE global shared by the hangar (Cache_ObjPlus0xBD8_To_dword_186BE8 @ 0x7afec, cached from the slot panel), the buy/sell screen (its panel A cache handler installed in BuySellScreen_BuildPanels/BuildControls) and the transfer screen (Transfer_CacheSelIndex @ 0x96E30): every screen's arrow handler trusts whatever row another screen last cached, which is what makes row 0x96368 possible. The port gives each screen its own copy (planeScratch / buySellScratch / transferScratch / nResearchTopicRowCache), so a fresh transfer session starts the cursor at 0 instead of inheriting the shop's last row. Listed so the QoL pass sees the difference.
column5: Cache helper 0x7afec (hangar), 0x96E30 (transfer panel A install); readers 0x78B54 (buy/sell draw), 0x96368/0x9606c-side (transfer handlers); a single global at 0x186BE8 in the original

column4: The commit's craft-row pass queues the panel C craft id into site->anCraftIds[nCraftsQueued], clears the home hangar cell (0x97CCC) and unhomes the craft (bHomeBase := 255, 0x97CD4), but raises none of the counters the delivery obeys: Smap_GrantSiteRecovery's craft pass walks the SIGNED byte site->bRecoveredCraftCount @ 0x205, whose only increment in the binary is ValidateCapacity's own craft-staging branch (0x96604). When the pending row is a craft row but staging never took the craft branch -- exactly the case under the cursor pairing of row 0x96368, where staging a soldier on row N sets the cached craft row's panel E digit -- the id lands in the list, the count stays 0, the grant pass runs zero times, and the craft is silently lost when the record compacts (0x994C8). The ship's own 24-hour arrival path never sees it: bHomeBase 255 takes it out of every base scan.
column5: Commit body 0x97AA4..0x97E8C: STRH into (site+0x2D0 + 2*count), no STRB at (site+0x205) anywhere in the function; the only 0x205 writers in the binary are 0x96604 (+1), 0x9627C (-1) and the Init/teardown clears; the grant loop at 0x98B50+ iterates (char)*(site+517)

column4: The tile lookup indexes the pad as uWidth * y + x over its data pointer and LDRBs the result with no comparison against the pad width or height, so out-of-map coordinates read outside the image -- the save round trip left a restored marker at (-6000,-6000) and the test's alt-tilemap lookup crashed. The unchecked read is kept faithful; fixtures park contacts on real cells.
column5: 0x8217C LDR R0,=unk_186B74; LDR R0,[R0]; LDRH R3,[R0,#8] (uWidth); MUL R2,R3,R2; LDR R3,[R0,#0xC] (pData); ADD R3,R2,R3; LDRB R0,[R3,R1]; RET -- 36 bytes, one block, no CMP anywhere

column4: The ship records store their strateg index into Ship+0x38, but LoadGame's per-craft pass 0x44F7C..0x450E8 matches a craft whose entry sits at another position and never re-stores Ship+0x38, so the craft keeps the number its record carried; consumers that read it as a list index (the arrival dispatch re-reads it) work on the wrong entry.
column5: 0x40BA8 store to Ship+0x38 while reading the record; 0x44F7C..0x450E8 re-match entries with no store to Ship+0x38

column4: The mission-end arm reaches PtrArray_DeleteAll (0x3E154), which empties the strateg list without refreshing the mirror count cell nStrategItemCount @ 0x186530 the way StrategList_RemoveAt does at 0x82B2C/0x82B34, so after Tact_Shutdown(1) the count cell names items that no longer exist and Save_WriteStrateg's loop 0x3FE28 would write records for them. The port re-states the cell at the save boundary; test_geoscapeframe section 17 asserts the stale value.
column5: 0x3E154 BL to the DeleteAll callee with no store to 0x186530 on any Tact_Shutdown arm; 0x82B2C/0x82B34 store the refreshed count inside RemoveAt

column4: The reinforcement arm increments nEnemyUnitCount before Map_PickRmpSpawnForUnit @ 0x55418 has accepted any node and ignores the pick failure; the consumers at 0x49260, 0x4C8D4 and 0x4CBE0 dereference the cell pointer with no test, so on shipped data (no bFlag20 == 4 node for rank-8 aliens, and Xcom-base reinforcements) a cell-less alien joins the roster. The port guards the consumer sites instead of reproducing the fault.
column5: 0x4BA3C count increment before the 0x55418 pick; 0x49260/0x4C8D4/0x4CBE0 cell dereferences with no test

column4: The phase-3 probe (0x39F24..0x39F50) and the init deploy-point sweep (0x3CC38) name cells by flat arithmetic on the 14400-slot pointer table and neither arm tests validity; Unit_PlaceOnMap (0x49B2C) resolves the target the same way. With the craft pad on the last map row the deploy offsets run past 10*dimY and the squad is parked in the NEXT layer's allocated cells, which the iso pass paints at the map edge. Reproduced on purpose through Init_LookupCellFlat (pufo_tactinit.c) with the found test as the occupant alone (0x39F50); asserted in test_geoscapeframe 100.5 (no crew cell ends NULL; six of the eight crew land on layer-2 cells whose own rows are 0..2 because the flat index passed row 59).
column5: Raw ARM phase 3 at 0x39F24..0x39F50, the init sweep at 0x3CC38, and placement at 0x49B2C use flat table arithmetic. tests/test_geoscapeframe.c:20056-20124 checks the injected deployment lookup, non-NULL crew cells, and a within-table next-layer wrap.

column4: Past the pointer table's own end (flat index >= 14400) the original reads the globals that sit behind Map+0x23438 -- Map_apTactItems onward -- and uses whatever it finds as a MapCell pointer. The port's flat twin refuses (returns NULL) and the deploy's found test then treats that point as taken. Recorded so an out-of-table coordinate path is never mistaken for parity.
column5: The recorded original access is past Map+0x23438. The port callback returns NULL when nIndex is outside 0..14399 (src/pufo/game/pufo_tactinit.c:80-92). test_geoscapeframe.c:20115-20124 covers a next-layer wrap still inside the allocation, not an index past the table.

column4: The flood head admits an occupant unless its nUnitType is 16 or 17 (0x27D18), while the walker's own step arm refuses any foreign occupant, so a planned route through an alien-held cell stalls the walk mid-path. The original stalls the same way. Reproduced (MoveStep's pTo->pUnit test, pufo_tactstate.c) and asserted in test_geoscapeframe's tact_play walk, which re-presses the target like a player does.
column5: The original head gate at 0x27CF0..0x27D18 admits only unit types 16 and 17; the port planner is src/pufo/game/pufo_step.c:739-800, while MoveStep separately rejects a foreign pTo occupant (src/pufo/game/pufo_tactstate.c:705-756). tests/test_geoscapeframe.c:16340-16365 re-presses and asserts final walk completion but does not require nStalls > 0, so occurrence of the exact mid-path stall is unverified.

column4: The read path takes the file's own first four bytes as the directory entry count with no guard (ReadFile at 0x9EFE8, result unchecked) and sizes the table with a 32-bit MUL at 0x9EFF4: the shipped cab manifest 0000SKKV.000's header count 1162040141 wraps to 0xAE0C4E51 = 2,928,006,481 before the throwing operator new at 0x9EFF8, a size a WinCE device cannot give, so the original ends the process when a load is pointed at a foreign file. The port's multiply widens to 64-bit in the same expression and asks 24,402,842,961 (measured with _msize in the test rather than assumed); its allocation then either fails (open false, pDir NULL) or succeeds and the 0x9F030 scan finds the manifest's empty first slot with nCurEntry 0. No save chunk is reachable either way. Asserted against the real original bytes in test_save.c TestForeignSaveBytes. The deviation is the request width and the refusal shape, not the outcome.
column5: The recorded raw read at 0x9EFE8 feeds a 32-bit MUL at 0x9EFF4 before the allocation at 0x9EFF8. tests/test_save.c:4476-4558 stages the original 359-byte manifest, checks its header count, measures the port allocation when available, and asserts that no save chunk is reached. The port uses a widened size_t product at src/pufo/dat/pufo_dat.c:153-158.

column4: The original clears the pocket/belt/backpack item slots, sets apBackpack[5] = apBackpack[6] = &unk_138EA0, and calls Unit_RecalcInventoryStat itself. The port does the type-armour pair and the armor constant only and leaves the recalc to its callers, so a new caller that trusts the original's shape carries stale items. Nothing is red today: each of the three call sites in pufo_tactctl.c recalcs what it needs.
column5: 0x498B0 item-slot clear, the apBackpack[5]/[6] = unk_138EA0 stores, and the internal Unit_RecalcInventoryStat call

column4: The four addresses an earlier PLAN row called 'caption buffers with no writer anywhere in the binary' are lang.dat text records: 0xEF024 = TEXTS[1188] aTextPsiColumnCaptions, 0xEF0F1 = TEXTS[1189] aTextSelectBase, 0xEF1BE = TEXTS[1190] aTextNoPsiRoom, 0xEBF4B = TEXTS[1127] aTextOk. PsiScreen_Draw loads the text block base at 0x72664 (LDR R11,=0xB38D0) and reads each caption as base + 205 * record, so the writer is the text loader and the strings are not empty.
column5: 0xB38D0 base load at 0x72664; the offsets 243540 / 243745 / 243950 / 231035 are exact multiples of the 205-byte record stride; 0 store references on all four, which is what a read-only text record looks like

column4: The colour-pair divisor is re-read from the global on every call: 0x2d860 loads Map_nGamma (Map+0x15100) and 0x2D870..0x2D8A8 turn it into 0.1*gamma+0.7 (0.1 at 0x2D878/0x2D880, 0.7 at 0x2D890/0x2D898), the pair held in R4/R5 for all six channel divisions in the helper with over 100 call sites; Map_InitAndLoadRegistry @ 0x22648 fills that dword at 0x227A0 from the registry "gamma" with the default 2 (the fallback MOV at 0x22794). Part 112 ports the mechanism: GfxColorEnv carries a POINTER to the live cell and World_NewGame / World_LoadSlot point it at the world's Map+0x15100 mirror, so a packed colour divides by the gamma the run has. The residue is a fixture value, not a mechanism: test_geoscapeframe boots on a zeroed PufoOptions (nGamma 0, nGameSpeed 0, volumes 0) where the app boots on the registry defaults 2, 4 and 5.
column5: 0x2d858 MOV R12,#(Map_nGamma-0x1139B8) then 0x2d860 LDR R0,[R6,R12]; A/B 2026-10-22: with the install removed the nine committed e2e pictures return byte-identical, and six of them move again when it is put back

column4: The original tests neither reader result: 0x3E49C BL AssetReader_Find is followed straight by MOV R2,#0x300 at 0x3E4A0 and 0x3E4AC BL AssetReader_Read, and 0x3E4B0 starts the conversion -- R0 is never read. Read's own refusal leaves the handle untouched and the 768-byte stack buffer as it was (bFound test at 0x9F8DC/0x9F8E8, bound test at 0x9F8F8/0x9F900, both landing on the epilogue at 0x9F950), so a missing .pal converts whatever the stack held and stores 256 entries of it. The port returns on either failure and stores nothing. Second half: the store index is (i + (slot & 0xFF) * 256) * 4 over the 0x1472D0 base -- AND R11,R4,#0xFF at 0x3E568, ADD R11,R0,R11,LSL#8 at 0x3E56C, STR R1,[R2,R11,LSL#2] at 0x3E570 -- i.e. 256 slots of 256 entries, while the port has PUFO_PAL_SLOTS 64 and masks & 63.
column5: 0x3E49C..0x3E4B0 has no branch on either result; MOV R1,#0x100 / CMP R0,R1 / BCC 0x3E588..0x3E590 is the 256-entry loop; 0x3E568/0x3E56C/0x3E570 is the slot math. Neither half is reachable in the app: every call site passes a slot <= 31 (the largest is 0x1F at 0x381A4) and main.dat holds every .pal the run asks for, so no frame moves. tests/test_render.c:TestPaletteDispatch pins the format order (0x40 555 first at 0x3E4C4..0x3E4CC, then 0x80 at 0x3E500, then 0x100 at 0x3E53C) and the slots the load does not touch.

column4: Two pen bounds are not the port's. penY < 0 with a non-zero index jumps back to 0xA424C having advanced nothing (CMP R5,#0 at 0xA42A4, BLT at 0xA42A8): the record keeps being read and nothing moves, a spin. penY >= nSurf1 ENDS the glyph -- CMP R5,R7 at 0xA42BC, BGE to the POP at 0xA42DC -- so the rest of the record is never consumed. The port skips-and-advances when penY < 0 and keeps consuming the record past nSurf1, drawing nothing out of bounds either way.
column5: 0xA42A4/0xA42A8 (spin), 0xA42BC/0xA42C0 -> POP 0xA42DC (glyph ends), store LDR palBase+val*4 at 0xA42C4 then STRH into blitState.pSrc at 2*(nSurf0*penY+penX) (0xA42CC). Only a hand-made record reaches either arm: byte 0 carries the start Y and 0xFE (0xA425C, penY +1 at 0xA4260) is the only penY change, so penY < 0 needs a negative start byte. tests/test_font.c:TestBlitGlyphPair feeds records the loader shape allows and the drawn pixels are identical in both.

column4: The release frees the pixel buffer and leaves the field pointing at it. LDR R0,[R0,#0xC] at 0x11010, CMP #0 at 0x11014, BLNE operator delete at 0x11018, POP {PC} at 0x1101C: no store back, so a pad released here still carries the freed pointer and any later PadImage_Blit @ 0x110dc or PadImage_BlitEx @ 0x11110 reads the record header and the pixels out of freed memory. The same shape shows up in UiControl_FreePads @ 0x1a2c8, which deletes the pads and then leaves the apPads slots pointing at deleted records. The port nulls pData, and nulls each slot it releases.
column5: 0x11010..0x1101C is the whole function body -- one load, one test, one conditional delete, and the return; there is no store anywhere in it. In the shipped run no pad is released and then drawn: the three release sites are UiControl_FreePads (through UiBank_FreeAllPads @ 0x1117c and the atexit thunk) and PadImage_Load @ 0x11020's own free-before-load, and in both the record is not blitted again. tests/test_render.c:TestPadImageRecord and tests/test_control.c:TestFreePads pin the port's null store, which the mutation case PadImage_FreeData-0x1100c-no-null shows the checks can see.

column4: Three shapes are not the port's. (1) The OLD buffer is freed at 0x1103C..0x11044 BEFORE the member is looked up, so when the member is missing the record ends with a NULL +0xC and with uWidth/uHeight/nMode holding the previous load's values -- the miss branch at 0x1108C jumps straight to the epilogue and none of the stores at 0x1109C/0x110C0/0x110C8/0x110CC runs. (2) Neither reader result is tested: AssetReader_Find at 0x1107C and AssetReader_Read at 0x110B4 both return values no instruction reads (the only test is AssetReader_Found's byte at 0x11084/0x11088), and a short read still leaves the full-size allocation in place. (3) The name is copied into a stack buffer by a byte loop at 0x11054..0x11064 with no length bound, and the allocation result is stored at 0x1109C with no null test. The port truncates the name, bounds the buffer and reports failure.
column5: Body order: 0x11038 Clear, 0x1103C/0x11040/0x11044 free-the-old, 0x11054..0x11064 the copy loop (MOVS R3,R1 / BNE), 0x11068..0x11070 strcat ".pad", 0x1107C Find, 0x11084 Found, 0x11088 ANDS/BEQ to 0x110D0, 0x11098 new(size), 0x1109C STR [R4,#0xC], 0x110B4 Read, 0x110BC..0x110CC the three field stores. Reach in the shipped run: every .pad the game asks for is in main.dat, so the miss arm never runs and no frame moves; the names handed in are 4-8 characters (invv, cursor, emptyb), far under the buffer. tests/test_render.c:TestPadImageRecord pins the u16 pair and the mode byte against a member the loader really reads, and refuses a missing member.

column4: Releases each of the three pads twice -- PadImage_FreeData for the pixel buffer and operator delete for the record itself -- and never clears the apPads slot, so a control that has been freed keeps three dangling pointers at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1C. UiBank_FreeAllPads @ 0x1117c runs this over all 130 bank widgets at exit. The port releases only the pixel data, NULLs the slot, and leaves the record to its owner because the port hands out caller-owned pads.
column5: Three LDR/CMP pairs at 0x1A2D0/0x1A2D4, 0x1A2F4/0x1A2F8, 0x1A318/0x1A31C; the FreeData calls at 0x1A2E8/0x1A30C/0x1A330 and the deletes at 0x1A2F0/0x1A314/0x1A338; the function writes nothing back into the control. The dangling slots are only read again if a control is blitted or reused after FreePads, which the shipped run does not do -- FreePads runs from the atexit path and from the screen-release paths that drop the control with it. tests/test_control.c:TestFreePads pins the port's NULL stores and that the pad records themselves survive.

column4: The constructor publishes seven fields and never writes the click handler at +0xC. It stores width and height as 16-bit 10 (MOV R2,#0xA at 0x1A290, STRH at 0x1A2A8 and 0x1A2AC), bEnabled at 0x1A2B0, bUnk17 at 0x1A2B4 and three pad slots as zero at 0x1A2B8/0x1A2BC/0x1A2C0. For the 130 bank widgets that is harmless -- they live in the static bank block at 0xAC6D0, which the image zeroes -- but a control built on operator new(0x20) inherits whatever the heap held at +0xC until a Setup writes a handler. The port stores NULL.
column5: Whole body: 0x1A290 MOV R2,#0xA, 0x1A2A8/0x1A2AC the two STRH, 0x1A2B0/0x1A2B4 the two bytes, 0x1A2B8/0x1A2BC/0x1A2C0 the three zero stores, and no store to +0xC anywhere in 0x1A28C..0x1A2C4. The only handlers a control gets are the ones Ui_InitTransfer @ 0x9955c, Ui_InitBaseInfo @ 0x9de5c and the other Setup paths install. tests/test_control.c pins the seven published fields; the mutation case UiControl_ctor-0x1a28c-width shows the width is checked.

column4: Every mode except 2 adopts pad 1's size, and the pad is loaded with no test: LDRNE R1,[R0,#0x18] at 0x1A5E0 is followed straight by the width read from pad+8 (stored at 0x1A5E8) and the height read from pad+0xA (stored at 0x1A5EC), so a control whose pad 1 was never loaded takes its size from address 0x8/0xA. The port tests the pad and keeps the control's own size when it is NULL.
column5: Order in the body: STRH [R0,#2] (y) at 0x1A5C8, CMP R2,#2 at 0x1A5D8, STRH [R0] (x) at 0x1A5DC, LDRNE 0x1A5E0 with the two size stores at 0x1A5E8/0x1A5EC, nMode at 0x1A5F0, the STRHNE size store at 0x1A5F8, nState at 0x1A5FC. Reach: the only call sites are UiControl_Setup paths, and their UiControl_LoadPads runs first (0x1A77C), so pad 1 is loaded for every descriptor that names it; the descriptors that name one pad leave slot 1 NULL and take the 0x8/0xA read. tests/test_control.c pins the mode-2 keeps-its-size rule and the pad-1 size adoption.

column4: Four gates the port dropped, and one field the original keeps. The whole body runs only when bInited is set (0x46154..0x4615C), so a second call does nothing at all. The per-slot loop runs only while nSlotCount is non-zero (0x46160..0x46168, counter 0x461A4/0x461A8), so a font that was loaded but has a zero count releases nothing. apSprData[i] is deleted with no null test (0x46180) while apMc1Data[i] is deleted only after CMP #0 (0x46190). The two index tables are released together behind a test on apSprIndex alone (0x461AC), so an apMc1Index allocated without its pair leaks. Finally only bInited is cleared (0x461D0): nSlotCount, nTotalSprFrames and nTotalMc1 keep their values. The port releases unconditionally, NULLs everything and clears the counts.
column5: 0x46154..0x4615C bInited gate; 0x46160..0x46168 count gate; 0x46180 delete with no test; 0x46190 delete after CMP #0; 0x461AC/0x461B4 the apSprIndex test with the deletes at 0x461B8 and 0x461C8; 0x461D0 the single flag clear. In the run the font is initialised once (Font_Init @ 0x460e8 through Font_RegisterAtexit's thunk at 0x460E0) and released once at exit, so no arm is reached twice. tests/test_font.c:TestFontInitFreeAndIndex pins the port's unconditional release and count clear, and names the three dropped gates on the check text.

column4: No bound of any kind: MOV R2,#0x594 at 0x46600 loads the index-table pointer field, the u16 argument is widened by LSL#16/LSR#16 (0x46608, 0x46610), and LDR R0,[R2,R3,LSL#2] at 0x46614 fetches the entry and RET at 0x46618 returns it. An index past the allocated table returns a pointer from whatever follows it, and the caller then draws through it. The port returns NULL past the count.
column5: Six instructions, no compare, no branch. The count the port keeps (nMc1IndexCount) is written by Font_BuildIndex @ 0x46480, which the original also has -- it just never consults it here. Reach: every caller passes an index it took from the same table family (the tactical sprite bases Font_LoadTactSprites @ 0x257c4 publishes), so an out-of-range index needs a corrupted or oversized SPR/MC1 member. tests/test_font.c pins the port's bound.

column4: Frees exactly nLineCount line pointers through the 4-byte stride and leaves apLines itself and every slot past the count in place: the line area of the block is 0xBE4 = 761 dwords, so slots past the count hold whatever the allocation held -- uninitialised for an operator new(0x1BB4) panel, zero for the static gUiRootPanel -- and a panel freed here still points at its freed line array. The port NULLs each slot it frees and stops at the same count.
column5: The loop bound is the panel's own count field, not a capacity constant, and the function writes no zero back into the block. Nothing draws a freed panel: the release sites are the screen teardowns, which drop the panel record with it. tests/test_panel.c pins the stop-at-count rule (a planted slot 5 survives a four-line free), and the mutation case FreeLines-0x3e8c8-bound shows the check sees a loop that runs to the capacity.

column4: The category panel is chosen through a signed byte with no bound: LDRSB R3,[R0] of g_nUfopaediaCategory at 0x99F9C (0x99FB8 for the back twin) and LDR R0,[R0,R3,LSL#2] over g_apUfopaediaCatPanels at 0x99FA4 (0x99FC0), with the scroller reached by tail call at 0x99FA8 (0x99FC4). The array holds nine pointers, and a category byte above 8 -- or negative, since the load is signed -- selects a pointer outside the nine and the scroller is then called on whatever that address holds. The port bounds the index and scrolls nothing when it is out of range.
column5: 0x99F98 and 0x99FB4 are five instructions each and contain no range test. The category byte is written by Ufopaedia_PrevEntry / Ufopaedia_NextEntry (0x9A06C and the walk), which wrap inside the nine categories, so the out-of-range arm needs a value no in-game path produces. tests/test_baseui.c pins the wiring (selector slots 6 and 7) and the nine category panels the builder allocates; the mutation cases ScrollPrevSel-0x99fb4-slot6 and ScrollNextSel-0x99f98-slot7 show the wiring checks have teeth.

column4: The five plain confirm bodies have no guard of any kind: 7 instructions (32-byte record with the =pBank pool word) that play Sound_Play(16,4) and tail-call Input_OnConfirm @ 0x15f3c with R0 = the bank pointer itself, loaded at 0x196F8 (0x19894, 0x198B4, 0x19920, 0x1A024 for the other four). The port's MenuBtn_Confirm guards `pCtx == NULL || pCtx->pState == NULL` and splits the bank into (TactInputState *, TactInputHooks *), so it can return early where the original cannot.
column5: 0x196e8, 0x19884, 0x198a4, 0x19910 and 0x1a014 were diffed position by position and are byte-identical; none of the six bodies (ConfirmSnd15 @ 0x198f0 included) contains a test or a branch. The port arm that differs needs a click whose state pointer is NULL -- every widget the bank installs carries the bank, so no shipped run reaches it.

column4: None of the five speed bodies tests its index or level: 19 instructions (84 bytes) that play Sound_Play(17,4) at 0x18ED8, write the five pad bytes, and tail-call GameSpeed_Set with the level in R1 (0x18F14). The port's `ValidStep(nStep)` refusal of a step outside 0..4 is therefore port-side behaviour the original does not have.
column5: Measured by mutation: dropping ValidStep from Menu_SetSpeed changed no check in any suite, because GameSpeed_Set bounds the level itself -- the 'step 5 refused' check is pinned by GameSpeed_Set, not by the menu guard. The originals get their level from the widget table (MOV R1,#0..#4), so an out-of-range level is a state the original is never in.

column4: 18 instructions (84 bytes) each, with no bounds test and no Sound_Play: Map_nMusicVolume @ 0x128a98 gets the immediate 1..5 (0x19A24 .. 0x19B74), Sound_ApplyMusicVolume @ 0x9e454 is called (0x19A28 .. 0x19B78), and the five music pads unk_AD09A..unk_AD11A are written one-hot. The port refuses a step outside 0..4 before doing any of it.
column5: The pad index is the value minus one and the value is the widget's own immediate, so a step of 5 or -1 is not a state the original can be in; the port guard is extra. Removing it would light a pad outside the five-pad group -- which is what the port's Pad_Lit guard exists to prevent.

column4: Same guard deviation as the music family, and the same shape with one extra call: 21 instructions (96 bytes) that store 1..5 into Map_nSoundVolume @ 0x128a94, call Sound_ApplySfxVolume @ 0x9e4dc, write the five sfx pads unk_AD13A..unk_AD1BA, and then tail-call Sound_Play(16,4) (0x19C00 MOV R0,#0x10, 0x19C04 POP {LR}, 0x19C08 B Sound_Play). No test, no branch.
column5: The claim in the IDB note and in the port comment that this family ends with Sound_Play(17) was wrong and is corrected: 0x19C00 is 0xE3A00010 = MOV R0,#0x10. The family that really ends with 17 is OptionsScreen_SetSfxVol0..5 @ 0x6bc1c.. (0x6BC60 = MOV R0,#0x11). The port code used 16 (PUFO_MENU_SAMPLE_POST) all along, so no behaviour changed -- only the recorded claim.

column4: The pad store is unconditional: 0x19DD4 `STRB R1,[R0,#(bCtl88ForceNoDrag - 0xAC6D0)]` runs on both arms with whatever value the taken arm left in R1 -- 0x19DB8 MOVNE R1,#1 on the clear arm, 0x19DCC MOVEQ R1,#0 on the set arm -- so the widget state byte is always written and always the inverse of the new flag. The port writes the pad only `if (pPad != NULL)` and returns false when `pOpt == NULL`.
column5: 15 instructions, 80 bytes, and the only test is 0x19DA4 `ANDS R3,R1,#0xFF` on the flag byte itself. Note also that 0x19D94 `LDR R0,=Map_bTactFlag` is only the addressing base for the 0x150e4 delta to Map_bForceNoDrag @ 0x128a9c: Map_bTactFlag is never read here. The differing port arm needs a NULL pOpt or pPad, which the widget call site never supplies.

column4: There is no 'no callee' arm in the original: all seven bodies do `LDR R0,=MainMenu_pSlotCtx @ 0x156938` and BL LoadGame @ 0x44bbc (0x1A0D0/0x1A0D4) with the slot immediate in R1. The port's Menu_LoadSlot treats a NULL pfnLoadGame as a zero result, which lands in the failure arm (mode 2 stored, 2 returned).
column5: 11 instructions + 2 pool words = 52 bytes per member, differing only in `MOV R1,#0..#6` (0x1A0C8..0x1A200), with no branch other than the low-byte test at 0x1A0D8. The port's invented arm is checked in tests/test_menubtn.c ('a missing load hook counts as a failure'), not in the original.

column4: None of the six sfx bodies tests anything: 100 bytes = 23 instructions (2 of them 2-word MOV immediates) + 2 pool words, no branch anywhere. The volume is the member's own immediate (MOV R1,#0..#5 at +0x0C), the widget is LDR R3,[R1,#(aOptionsSfxBtn+4N-0x159E20)] at +0x24, the mute byte is #1 at step 0 and #0 at 1..5, then BL Sound_ApplySfxVolume at +0x3C, and sample 17 is played TWICE: MOV R1,#4 / MOV R0,#0x11 / BL Sound_Play at 0x6BC5C, 0x6BC60, 0x6BC64, then MOV R1,#4 / MOV R0,#0x11 / POP {LR} / B Sound_Play at 0x6BC68, 0x6BC6C, 0x6BC70, 0x6BC74. The port's Options_ClampStep is port-side behaviour the original does not have.
column5: The doubled play is the original's shape and the port had it wrong: OptionsScreen_SetSfxVol played 17 once and the IDB note at 0x6bc1c said 'tail-call Sound_Play(17)'. Both now say twice, and tests/test_baseui.c counts the plays ('muted plays nothing, a step plays 17 twice': 0 at step 0 because Sound_Play @ 0x9E10C tests Map_bSoundOff first, 2 at every other step). The clamp was measured, not assumed: replacing Options_ClampStep(nStep) with nStep in the music handler changed no check in any suite, because the widget table can only supply 0..5.

column4: Six members of 92/76/92/92/92/76 bytes = 20/17/20/20/20/17 instructions + 2 pool words (3/2/3/3/3/2 of the instructions are 2-word MOV immediates, which is why the byte totals exceed 4*count). No bounds test, no branch, and no Sound_Play -- that is what separates this group from the sfx one. Each member stores its own immediate into Map_nMusicVolume, calls ClearMusicButtons, lights one button, stores Map_bMusicOff = (N==0) and tail-calls B Sound_ApplyMusicVolume @ 0x9e454. The port adds Options_ClampStep, which the original has no equivalent of.
column5: The two code shapes are a codegen difference only: the 92-byte members reload Map_nMusicVolume and compute the widget pointer with ADD R3,R0,R1,LSL#2 (0x6BA3C..0x6BA48), the 76-byte members fold it into the immediate offset LDR [R1,#(aOptionsMusicBtn+4N-0x159E20)] (0x6BA94 for Vol1, 0x6BBF4 for Vol5). The index claim is pinned by mutations (apMusic[0] instead of the step fails 8 checks); the clamp itself is extra -- measured inert when removed.

column4: Each is 64 bytes = 15 instructions + 1 pool word: LDR R0, MOV R1,#0, six LDR/STRB pairs writing 0 into byte +10 of each widget pointer, RET. No widget pointer is ever tested -- 0x6B99C..0x6B9C8 and 0x6B9DC..0x6BA08 dereference whatever the array holds. The return value is a pointer, not a status: the last LDR reuses R0 (0x6B9C4 for music, 0x6BA04 for sfx) so RET returns the sixth widget. The port's OptionsScreen_ClearRadioGroup guards every slot with `apCtl[i] != NULL`.
column5: The pointer return is pinned (return apCtl[5] -> NULL fails 3 checks), the six-store claim is pinned (loop bound 6 -> 5 fails 7 checks). The port's NULL arm has no counterpart in the original: reaching it means a NULL slot in aOptionsMusicBtn/aOptionsSfxBtn, which the options bring-up at 0x6be84 fills first. Measured 2026-10-23.

column4: Both are 72 bytes = 14 instructions + 4 pool words: four panel slots loaded (0x6D020, 0x6D02C, 0x6D038, 0x6D044), each dereferenced and passed to DecDwordIfPos_AtPlus0xBD4 at 0x6D028, 0x6D034, 0x6D040 and the tail call at 0x6D050 after POP at 0x6D04C -- with no test on any slot. PanelNext is the mirror over IncDwordIfInRange_AtPlus0xBD4 @ 0x3f00c (0x6D070, 0x6D07C, 0x6D088, tail 0x6D094). The port wraps every call in `if (apPanels[i] != NULL)`, so it skips a slot where the original would dereference it.
column5: One press moves all four list cursors -- the 'four panels, one direction' claim is pinned by two mutations (bound 4 -> 3 fails 3 checks; ScrollNext -> ScrollPrev in PanelNext fails 6). The four slots are 0x159E18, 0x159E78, 0x159E7C and 0x159E1C, which the options bring-up fills (app/pufo_world.c:9123..9126), and these two handlers are only reachable from the built options screen (app/pufo_world.c:1778, 1785), so the original's unguarded dereference is never reached.

column4: Seven members of 76 bytes = 15 instructions + 4 pool words (sGeoscapeScreenBlock, gOptionsScratch, MainMenu_pSlotCtx, MainMenu_nListMode), differing only in `MOV R1,#0..#6` at +0x0C, with no test and no branch in any of them: MainMenu_nListMode = 4 at +0x10, BL SaveGame at +0x18 with its result discarded, byte_159E88[0] = 0 at +0x24, MainMenu_nListMode = 1 at +0x2C, POP at +0x34, tail B Geoscape_CloseUI at +0x38. The port's `pEnv == NULL` guard is invented; discarding SaveGame's result is faithful.
column5: Six mutations pin the order and the values: the mode-4 store moved after SaveGame fails 8 checks (g_nSlotListModeAtRender), the mode-1 store changed to 3 fails 8, the tab clear dropped fails 8, the close dropped fails 8, slot +1 fails 8. The port's NULL arm is checked in tests/test_baseui.c ('a null slot env saves nothing'), which is the port's rule and not the original's.

column4: Seven members of 104 bytes = 21 instructions + 5 pool words differing only in `MOV R1,#0..#6` at +0x38. The only test in the whole body is on the LOW BYTE of the result: ANDS R3,R0,#0xFF at +0x44, MOVEQ R0,#1 at +0x48, STREQ [MainMenu_nListMode] at +0x4C. Nothing is guarded, and the byte the handler raises at +0x28..+0x30 (LDR R0,=(gOptionsScratch+4); STRB R1,[R0]) is the same byte OptionsScreen_Init tests at 0x6BE84 -- so the load click FORCES OptionsScreen_Init's teardown branch even when the options screen was never built, and that branch frees pads and clears the flag on controls nobody constructed. The port's four guards (pDat, pLoadEnv, pnListMode, pbTab) are invented.
column5: Measured 2026-10-23, and it needed a fixture fix to see: the port's SaveSlotEnv.pbControlsExist and OptionsInitEnv.pbControlsExist are two pointer fields, and the test wired them to two different cells, so the causality between +0x30 and 0x6BE84 was invisible and the first-draft mutation of 0x6b2cc came out inert. Wiring them to one cell (which is what app/pufo_world.c:1728 and :9084 do for the real build) makes the same mutation fail 17 checks. The forced teardown is therefore a real original shape, not a port choice.

column4: 68 bytes = 14 instructions + 3 pool words. The one-shot gate is 0x99FD4 LDRB + 0x99FDC BNE, the flag is set at 0x99FE4, the slot is MOV R3,#0xBD0 then ORR R3,R3,#8 = 0xBD8 (0x99FE8, 0x99FF0), the row is read at 0x99FF8 and stored as a byte at 0x9A000. The RET at 0x9A004 returns whatever R0 holds at the end of the taken path: the caching path returns the ADDRESS of g_nUfopaediaCategory (R0 from 0x99FFC), the early exit returns the flag byte itself (R0 from 0x99FD4 LDRB) -- neither is a status a caller could use. The port returns a bool saying whether it cached.
column5: There is no direct call to 0x99fd0 anywhere: its three cross-references are the two handler stores inside Ufopaedia_Open @ 0x9a8cc (0x9A94C `LDR R2,=Ufopaedia_CacheSelRow` + `STR R2,[R0,R3]`, and 0x9AA4C) plus the pointer entry at 0x18AC50, i.e. it is installed as the selector panel's click handler at 0x9A958 and reaches its caller through the widget dispatcher. The port's own call site discards the result (`(void)Ufopaedia_CacheSelRow(...)`, app/pufo_world.c:8509) while tests/test_baseui.c checks the bool. The one-shot gate itself is pinned: setting the flag back to 0 fails 4 checks (a second call caches again and the row the rest of the ufopaedia code reads changes).

column4: 32 bytes = 8 instructions, no pool word: PUSH {R4,LR}, MOV R4,R1 at 0x6DD08, MOV R1,#4, MOV R0,#7, BL Sound_Play, MOV R0,R4, POP {R4,LR}, B OptionsScreen_Open. The first argument arrives in R0 and is never read -- 0x6DD08 keeps the SECOND argument and the tail call passes that as OptionsScreen_Open's mode. Sample 7 with 4 as its second argument, the same shape the other openers use.
column5: The port keeps the quirk on purpose (OptionsScreen_OpenWithSound(nIgnored, nMode, hooks)) and the sample id is pinned by a mutation: 7 -> 16 fails 2 checks. Recorded so that a later reader does not 'fix' the unused argument into something the original never had.

column4: The port's family comment said 'Thirteen thunks, one tail call' and called the copies byte-identical. Census over every function body, 2026-10-23: 25 bodies end `B Geoscape_CloseUI` @ 0x8b94c; 12 are this 12-byte shape -- 0x557bc 0x589c0 0x59b54 0x5abd8 0x5c078 0x64ae4 0x6e3d4 0x72ffc 0x75154 0x838d0 0x96020 0x9a8c0. Compared word by word those 12 share the LDR word E59F0000 and the DCD 0x1864F8 and differ ONLY in the branch-displacement word, so they are shape-identical, not byte-identical. The 'thirteen' counted NewBaseScreen_CloseThunk @ 0x615b0 with them; that record is 32 bytes and plays its own sample first.
column5: Word compare of the three words in each of the 12 records; census written into the IDB comment at 0x557bc, the port comment at pufo_baseui.c:3453 and the test comment at tests/test_baseui.c TestCloseThunks.

column4: Two notes on this record said 72 B = 17 instructions + 4 pool words. Walking it item by item gives 14 instructions + 4 pool words: PUSH, LDR, LDRB, ANDS, BNE, LDR, LDR, BL, LDR, MOV, STRB, LDR, POP, B, with pool 0x1864F8 0x159618 0x1863E8 0x158840 -- 14*4 + 4*4 = 72 exactly, so the old count was 12 bytes too many. The behaviour claim it carried (one byte test at 0x577C8..0x577D0 gating BOTH the strateg-list removal at 0x577D4 and the clock unpause at 0x577E0..0x577E8, both arms converging on 0x577F4) is unchanged.
column5: Branch displacement in the B at 0x577F4; the two pool words 0x159618 (nGameTotalSec, the GameTime block base) and 0x1863E8 (g_smapCamera, loaded at 0x577D8 and never read). IDB comment at 0x577c0 now lists the 14.

column4: The record is 32 B = 7 instructions + 1 pool word, not '8 insns, no pool': PUSH {LR} / MOV R1,#4 / MOV R0,#0x11 / BL Sound_Play @ 0x615BC / LDR R0,=sGeoscapeScreenBlock / POP {LR} / B Geoscape_CloseUI @ 0x615C8 / DCD 0x1864F8. The pool word is the block it hands the dispatcher, so the record is not pool-free; the POP sits between the block load and the tail call, which is why the tail still passes the argument.
column5: Measured 2026-10-23. Its doubled sample -- its own Sound_Play(17, 4) plus Geoscape_CloseUI's head play at 0x8B95C -- is pinned by tests/test_baseui.c TestCloseThunks, whose sample sink counts 2*17 here and 17 for each 12-byte copy; changing 17 to 18 there fails the count.

column4: The header called the transfer pair 'the same eleven instructions' and 'byte-identical' to BuySellScreen_PanelPrev @ 0x76088. The record is 88 B = 17 instructions + 5 pool words; word compare finds 5 of the 22 words different and all five are branch displacements (four BL plus the tail B), while the 17 instructions and the 5 pool words -- the same five pBuySellPanelA..E globals in the same load order -- are the same. The next pair (0x760e0 / 0x9683c) is the same case, and the hangar detail pair @ 0x79a70/0x79ac8 shares the shape with 10 words different (the 5 displacements plus 5 pool words naming other columns).
column5: Word compare 0x967e4 vs 0x76088 and 0x9683c vs 0x760e0 (slots 3, 6, 9, 12, 16). Pool order is reversed: 0x96828 = pBuySellPanelE ... 0x96838 = pBuySellPanelA while the body loads A first.

column4: Notes said the six weapon copies 'differ only in MOVNE R1,#0x19..#0x1E'. Consecutive 68-byte records differ in exactly 3 words: the two MOVNE immediates (slots 4 and 10, both columns get the same mount number) and the tail-B displacement. An earlier note also named the gate words as 0x79B6C and 0x79B80; the gates are A: LDRB 0x79B68 + ANDS 0x79B6C and B: LDRB 0x79B80 + ANDS 0x79B84.

column4: The header and the test carried this pair's globals as bare addresses (unk_161EDC, unk_161A3C) although the IDB already names them pPlaneCrewPanel @ 0x161EDC and pPlaneCrewStatusPanel @ 0x161A3C. The same held for the manuf tail (pManufPanelB/C/D @ 0x15EE48/0x15EE40/0x15EE38), the psi arrays (g_apPsiNamePanel @ 0x15EED0, g_apPsiStatPanel @ 0x15EE88, g_apPsiDeltaPanel @ 0x15EEA8, g_apPsiCheckPanel @ 0x15EE58, indexed by byte_1870F4) and the buy/sell five (pBuySellPanelA..E). column5: Pool words read out of each record: 0x79A40/0x79A44, 0x6DD84..0x6DD90, 0x71634..0x71644 (plus byte_1870F4 at 0x71644), 0x96828..0x96838, 0x72E5C..0x72E64, 0x79AB4..0x79AC4. column4: The port line reads `*pnBudget -= nDamage;  /* 0x57CE4 */`, which says the burn depends on the value passed in. In the record each defence pair burns a FIXED immediate: SUB #0x1F4 = 500 at 0x57CE0 (0x57CE4 is the STR that follows), SUB #0x258 = 600 at 0x57E8C, SUB #0x384 = 900 at 0x5803C, and 1500 built as MOV #0x5D0 / ORR #0xC at 0x581E0 with SUB R3,R2,R3 at 0x581EC. The gravity pair burns nothing: SUB R3,R3,R1 at 0x58390 is the pointer difference that opens the 'ALL RECHARGED' label copy, the same idiom as 0x58334 above it, and the pair leaves the budget cell [SP,#var_C0] alone. PUFO_BASEAT_DAMAGE_MISSILE/LASER/PLASMA/FUSION are 500/600/900/1500, so the behaviour matches; the comment is what was wrong.
column5: Disassembly of the four pair blocks 0x57BF8..0x583E0: the only SUB-with-immediate in each is the burn (0x57CE0, 0x57E8C, 0x5803C) and 0x581E0/0x581EC build 0x5DC = 1500 before the subtract. Mutation of the port line to `-= nDamage + 1` printed 0 failing checks, but not because nothing reads the budget: TestBaseAtUpdate already pins every burn with hit fixtures (tests/test_baseui.c:17689..17716) and the eight-class budget table (17717..17742). The +1 crosses none of them because each boundary is 'the budget reaches exactly 0' and 501 off 500 is still below 1. Part 134 closed it with -1 and +100 mutations and 8 interval checks.

column4: The teardown clear is cited as `memset(pSite->auItemQty, 0, sizeof(pSite->auItemQty)); /* 0x76C18 */`. 0x76C18 is `ADD R3, R0, #2`, the loop's START address, not a store: the clear is 256 x `STRH [R3],#2` at 0x76C20 (R2 = 0x100 at 0x76C08, SUBS/BPL at 0x76C24/0x76C28) over site+2..0x201. struct SmapSite puts auItemQty[256] at 0x002 with 512 bytes, so the memset covers exactly the same bytes and the order after it matches the ARM (bFlag0 0x000 at 0x76C30, bFlag1 0x001 at 0x76C38, uRecoveredSoldiers 0x202 at 0x76C3C with R3 = 0x200|2, 0x204 at 0x76C48, 0x205 at 0x76C4C, then the 100-entry u16 run from 0x208 at 0x76C50). The cite names the setup instruction; no behaviour differs.
column5: Disassembly 0x76C00..0x76C60. Mutating the memset length to `sizeof(...) - 2` printed 0 failing checks: no check reads the last slot of auItemQty, so the clear's extent is unpinned (PLAN row 133a). The case with teeth is the site's own flag byte at 0x76C30 -> 2 failing checks.

column4: InitInstance spends a warm-up and ten draws before it builds the asset paths: srand(100 * wSecond + wMilliseconds) @ 0xA00F8, then plain rand() wSecond times (0xA0108..0xA011C), then Game_RandU16 with the bounds 5, 3, [2 only when the 3-draw is NOT 1 -- 0xA0154 stores 0 and skips it], 8, 2, 4, 0x46, 0xC8, then the mission pick from 10, redrawn while it is 7.
